data.source_title: Role of Point-of-Care Testing in Reducing Time to Treatment Decision-Making in Urgency Patients: A Randomized Controlled Trial
data.locator: Table 3, Blood draw to complete laboratory time row and its footnote; Methods, Outcomes
data.source_setting: Siriraj Hospital Urgency Room, tertiary university hospital, Bangkok, Thailand; adults triage level 3/4 requiring electrolyte tests (Na, K, Cl, bicarbonate); single-center RCT.
data.source_n: 248 randomized patients: 124 point-of-care testing (POCT), 124 central-laboratory testing (CLT); 12 of 260 eligible declined.
data.quantity: Blood draw to all laboratory results reported, median (IQR)
data.source_evidence_basis: Table 3 separates two endpoints: the row “Blood draw to complete laboratory time” reports 72 min (POCT) and 87.5 min (CLT), medians (IQR), defined in the table footnote as blood draw until all results were reported. The separate “Laboratory turnaround time” rows report POCT 5 min (IQR 4–6) and CLT 87.5 min (IQR 70–103); the Methods defines lab TAT as sample accessing to results reporting.
data.limitations: Do not conflate Table 3’s distinct rows: POCT instrument/lab TAT is 5 min (IQR 4–6), while POCT blood-draw-to-all-results is 72 min (IQR 54.5–90). The CLT median is 87.5 in both rows, with IQR 70–103 in both rows. Selected adult urgency cohort at one Thai hospital.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Use as an external sensitivity range for a defined blood-draw-to-results event in comparable lower-acuity ED scenarios. Do not treat as local or universal; model POCT vs central lab as distinct branches and calibrate to local workflow.

data.source_title: Role of Point-of-Care Testing in Reducing Time to Treatment Decision-Making in Urgency Patients: A Randomized Controlled Trial
data.locator: Table 3, “Laboratory turnaround time”; Results, Primary outcomes
data.source_setting: Siriraj Hospital Urgency Room, tertiary university hospital, Bangkok, Thailand; adults triage level 3/4 requiring electrolyte tests (Na, K, Cl, bicarbonate); single-center RCT.
data.source_n: 248 randomized patients: 124 point-of-care testing (POCT), 124 central-laboratory testing (CLT); 12 of 260 eligible declined.
data.quantity: Laboratory turnaround time by method, median (IQR)
data.source_evidence_basis: Table 3, “Laboratory turnaround time” rows report POCT 5 min (IQR 4–6) and CLT 87.5 min (IQR 70–103); Methods defines general lab TAT as sample accessing to results reporting. The table separately reports a blood-draw-to-all-results interval of 72 min (IQR 54.5–90) for POCT and 87.5 min (IQR 70–103) for CLT.
data.limitations: The POCT analytical/lab TAT endpoint (5 min) differs from the separately reported POCT draw-to-all-results interval (72 min); do not combine them. Single-center selected cohort.
data.inferred_scenario_use: For an explicitly method-level modeling assumption only: vary a rapid point-of-care path around the reported 5-minute analytical interval versus central testing around 70–103-minute IQR. Keep collection, reporting and clinician review as separate modeled intervals.
